analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/reference/configuration.md (head text, no diff patch supplied) and a new, empty-text docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md. I could not isolate which lines changed in configuration.md, so I reviewed the visible config surface against the threat model.

Checked and consistent with the model:
- Endpoint-resumption and logout text (lines 67-88). Logout revokes against saved issuer metadata, with no config retargeting, which matches A-008 and T-053.
- Worker and native qualification flags (lines 127-143) are exact `1`, create no local trust and extend no proof lifetime, which matches TB-011.
- SSD cache TTL is capped at 1800 s (line 508), and `cache.directory` plus `volume_uuid` are checked (lines 489-493), consistent with T-041.
- `EnvironmentScrubber` removes DYLD and related variables (line 565).

Drift found, reported in findings: `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY`, the hybrid recurrent RAM bank and the MiMo complete-prefix gate (lines 349, 502, 531-532) document a resident prefix tier. T-041 says production has no RAM tier. Line 501's default-on-only-for-exact-cohorts also differs from T-041's default-on-for-every-eligible-model wording.

Coverage limits: the new Nemotron file has no text, so only its metadata was available, and metadata_citation_sides is empty. No code was supplied, so none of the doc claims about reading symbols or defaults could be checked against source. The pinned platform links were not reviewed.

findings.detail: The head text of configuration.md documents `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY` (line 502), forwarded by LaunchAgent. It is an explicit opt-in for paged resident blocks and the recurrent RAM bank. Lines 531-532 add hybrid recurrent-checkpoint retention through `DARKBLOOM_CBV2_HYBRID_PREFIX_*`, and line 349 adds a MiMo complete-prefix gate. T-041's mitigations state that production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache and that there is no production RAM tier or tier composition. T-041 also describes the SSD tier as default-on for every eligible CBv2 model, whereas line 501 says the default is on only for exact cohorts. A provider operator who sets the memory opt-in gets a shared-across-tenants resident cache. It carries the same TTFT hit/miss oracle (SEC-035, leak #1) with no TTL, no HMAC-keyed names and no at-rest encryption story. Those controls are only analysed for the SSD tier. I could not see the diff, so I cannot say whether this tier was introduced by this PR. Fix: update T-041 to cover the opt-in resident tier. State its salt scoping and lifetime, whether in-memory data is cleared on unload, and the exact default-on cohort. Or correct the docs if the tier is not reachable in production.
findings.title: Threat model T-041 says no production RAM prefix tier exists, but the config reference documents an opt-in resident tier forwarded to launchd
